subject.title: feat(agents): Swarm core — collector spawn, agents_wait, structured output, caps (gated)

question: Should the default-off `tools.swarm` configuration, new `agents_wait` tool contract, and additive persisted collector record be accepted as OpenClaw’s permanent core orchestration surface after the terminal-error repair?
rationale: The patch adds a broad, compatibility-sensitive core feature whose API, configuration, protocol, and persisted-state semantics exceed a mechanical defect fix; the maintainer label requires explicit sponsorship despite the frozen implementation spec.

options.title: Sponsor the gated core contract
options.body: Repair failed-collector diagnostics, keep the feature default-off, and approve the documented config, tool, protocol, and storage contract with real enabled-path evidence.

options.title: Narrow the first landing
options.body: Land only a smaller internally scoped collector primitive and defer public config, catalog, and gateway exposure until the permanent API is agreed.

options.title: Pause the core feature
options.body: Keep the Swarm work out of core until a maintainer confirms that this orchestration capability belongs in the product roadmap.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the gated core contract
recommendation.body: Repair failed-collector diagnostics, keep the feature default-off, and approve the documented config, tool, protocol, and storage contract with real enabled-path evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked program issue and the proposed specification identify steipete as the person currently carrying the Swarm design and implementation boundary.
